question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 y^{3}}{x^{2} y + x y^{2}}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2 y^{3}}{x^{2} y + x y^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{2 v^{3} x^{3}}{v^{2} x^{3} + v x^{3}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{2 v^{2}}{v + 1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2 v^{2}}{v + 1} - v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v^{2} - v}{v + 1} \\ \left(\frac{v + 1}{v^{2} - v}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=e^{\sin{\left(\frac{3 y}{x} \right)}}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =e^{\sin{\left(\frac{3 y}{x} \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =e^{\sin{\left(3 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =e^{\sin{\left(3 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- v + e^{\sin{\left(3 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- v + e^{\sin{\left(3 v \right)}} \\ \left(- \frac{1}{v - e^{\sin{\left(3 v \right)}}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\tan{\left(\frac{x^{2}}{y^{2}} \right)} + \frac{4 y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\tan{\left(\frac{x^{2}}{y^{2}} \right)} + \frac{4 y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =4 v + \tan{\left(\frac{1}{v^{2}} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =4 v + \tan{\left(\frac{1}{v^{2}} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =3 v + \tan{\left(\frac{1}{v^{2}} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =3 v + \tan{\left(\frac{1}{v^{2}} \right)} \\ \left(\frac{1}{3 v + \tan{\left(\frac{1}{v^{2}} \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{6 x^{2} + y^{2}}{x y}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{6 x^{2} + y^{2}}{x y} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{v^{2} x^{2} + 6 x^{2}}{v x^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{v^{2} + 6}{v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- v + \frac{v^{2} + 6}{v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{6}{v} \\ \left(\frac{v}{6}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
